# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel only the large button and three wire positions; the printed “PUSH TO DEFUSE” is not tactile information for me. I need the Mute to relay the manual’s rules and the Deaf’s visual readings. I’m establishing a simple relay request now rather than attempting any action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I feel one large button and three wire positions, but no wire properties. Please read the manual and relay its exact defusal rule. Also establish a small code with Deaf: have Deaf report DISPLAY, LIGHT, BUTTON, and each wire using gestures that you describe to me in your next spoken turn.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝"])
wait()
```

No information has reached me yet. Since I cannot see gestures, the Mute must read the manual and communicate its rule to the Deaf through gestures; the Deaf can then speak the rule to me. I am asking both to use that relay and not touch or activate anything.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please read the manual now. You cannot speak, so use gestures to relay its complete rule to Deaf; Deaf should then say the rule aloud to me on the next round. Include any required display, light, button, or wire conditions.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "☝"])
wait()
```

The board still gives me no tactile facts beyond the button and wire positions, and no relay has arrived. I’m specifying a compact protocol: Mute can read the manual, encode its findings in gestures, and Deaf can decode them and speak them to me. The numeric gestures will identify wire positions; the remaining gestures identify yes/no and the three visible fields.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use this relay protocol to Deaf, then Deaf speak the decoded result to me: 👍 means YES, 👎 means NO, 👆 means DISPLAY, ✌ means LIGHT, 👌 means BUTTON, ✊ means WIRE, and for a wire use [✊, position gesture], with position 1=☝, 2=✌, 3=🤟. Send the manual rule as these tokens and include each condition's value. Deaf, please speak the decoded manual rule and your visual readings to me.")
wait()
```

The Deaf reports the visual facts: display 0, yellow light, and wires red at 1, blue at 2, green at 3. The earlier relay suggests the manual says to cut the blue wire, but its ending was unclear, so I should not cut yet. I am asking the Mute for exact confirmation; no physical action is safe until that arrives.

```

```

Deaf says to Blind: I cannot verify Mute's gesture code or a safe action. Do not cut a wire or press the button based on my messages; require Mute's exact manual instruction.

The Deaf cannot certify the earlier interpretation, so I will require a direct, unambiguous gesture sequence from the Mute. The agreed code is: ✊ means cut, 👌 means press, and the second symbol gives the wire position—☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3. Mute should send exactly one action sequence; Deaf should report the observed symbols literally and then their decoded meaning.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Send Deaf exactly one gesture sequence for the final action: ✊ then ☝, ✌, or 🤟 means cut wire 1, 2, or 3; 👌 means press the button. Do not add other symbols. Deaf, report the literal symbols you see and the decoded action.")
wait()
```

The available relay is still ambiguous, so I will not act. I am reducing the action code to one unmistakable gesture, with no position word or extra symbols: ✊ means cut wire 1, 👊 means cut wire 2, 🤛 means cut wire 3, and 👌 means press the button. Mute must send exactly one of these; Deaf should report the single symbol literally and its decoded action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture exactly one symbol for the manual's final action, with no extras: ✊ means cut wire 1; 👊 means cut wire 2; 🤛 means cut wire 3; 👌 means press button. Deaf, report exactly the one symbol you see and its decoded action. Do not rely on the earlier message.")
wait()
```

The latest relay is still not an actionable, verified instruction. I will keep the bomb untouched and give Mute a simpler protocol with a single legal gesture and no multi-symbol sequence: if the manual says cut wire 2 (the blue wire), Mute must gesture 👊 exactly once; if it says press, Mute must gesture 👌 exactly once. ``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send words or multiple gestures. If the exact manual instruction is cut wire 2, gesture 👊 exactly once. If it is press the button, gesture 👌 exactly once. Deaf, report the one literal symbol received.")
